examples.knowledge_point: Utilizing the Oddness Property of the Cosecant Function
examples.problem: If $\csc{x} = \dfrac{7}{2},$ then find the value of $\csc(-x - 20\pi).$
examples.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the graph of $y = \csc{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13940224/assets/a8e7894ea970c539ca59a73713fa15450f4361b3fc8bc22183e3fe84946411bd.png)

From the graph, we note the following:

- The period of $\csc{x}$ is $2\pi.$

- Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. This means that $\csc{x}$ is an *odd* function, and we have

$$
\csc(-x) = -\csc{x}.
$$

Let's now evaluate our expression:

- Firstly, using the periodicity of $\csc{x},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{csc}⁡(-x-20\pi ) & =\operatorname{csc}⁡(-x-2\pi \cdot 10) \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡(-x).\end{aligned}
$$

- Secondly, using the oddness of $\csc{x},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{csc}⁡(-x) & =-\operatorname{csc}⁡x \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\csc(-x - 20\pi) = -\dfrac{7}{2}.$

feedback.worked_solution:
The period of $y=\operatorname{csc}⁡x$ is $2\pi .$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\operatorname{csc}⁡(x+2n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=-2$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\operatorname{csc}⁡(x+2\cdot (-2)\cdot \pi )=\operatorname{csc}⁡(x-4\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=2,$ then $\operatorname{csc}⁡(x-4\pi )=2.$

Finally, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{csc}⁡(x-4\pi )+2 & =\frac{1}{4}(2)+2 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+2 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
